subject: Skyward: request for safety-net deposit, termination rights, and cash remedies
messages:
From: Elena Ramirez <elena.ramirez@skyward.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, procurement@skyward.io
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood SLA asks — escrow + termination safety net

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the standard SLA language and have two non-negotiable asks that we need to resolve before legal can proceed:

1) Fee-at-risk / escrow: Skyward needs a mechanism to recover cash for repeated P1/P2 breaches instead of only credits. Specifically we want a 6-figure escrow (tiered by ARR) or an alternative cash-withdrawal mechanism tied to severity breaches.

2) Termination trigger: if Redwood misses the P1 latency SLA (99.9% > 150ms) in two consecutive months, Skyward must have a right to terminate for convenience with a pro-rated refund of prepaid fees and a capped buyout equal to 2x monthly committed fees.

We understand this is outside your standard terms, so we sent the attached "Skyward_SLA_asks_v2.pdf" with proposed language. Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept an escrow-based holdback or, alternately, a liquidated damages schedule? If not, please propose a compromise we can run past legal.

Elena
Elena Ramirez
Head of Procurement, Skyward
elena.ramirez@skyward.io

Subject: Re: Redwood SLA asks — escrow + termination safety net

Hi Elena — really appreciate the clear asks and the attached doc. Short answer: we understand why Skyward is asking for stronger cash remedies; Reducing customer risk is important. Long answer: the standard Redwood position for commercial customers is to offer SLA credits and a capped liability linked to fees, with narrow termination rights. That said, for strategic customers we can consider structured alternatives.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in Legal and our Contracts SME (cc'd) to scope a negotiable approach.
- Can you share the ARR band and an example committed monthly spend so we can model an escrow size?
- We'll propose a staged compromise that preserves availability incentives while limiting Redwood's systemic exposure.

I expect to follow up with a written counterproposal by EOD Wednesday. In the meantime, we reviewed the attached ask and have two initial alternative options we think are workable:

A) SLO Reserve + Termination Gate: A percentage reserve (held in a short-term escrow account) equal to 1–3 months of committed fees by ARR band. Reserve funds are released gradually; funds can be drawn down to cover remediation and capped buyout payments after a cure window and repeated P1 failures. Termination allowed after 2 consecutive months of qualifying P1 breaches with a capped buyout equal to X months of committed fees (propose X=3 for high-ARR tiers).

B) Severity-indexed Liquidated Damages: No open-ended escrow; instead, a defined LD schedule where repeated P1/P2 breaches escalate cash payouts up to a fixed cap (e.g., up to 6 months of fees over a 12-month period). Includes a cure period and requirement to use alternate region/variant before termination.

Would either of those map to what procurement needs to sign off? Happy to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

----- My notes -----
- Risk exposure: Skyward asks significantly increase our near-term cash exposure. We should avoid long-tail, unlimited LD.
- Escrow practicality: Setting up a third-party escrow is operationally heavy but doable for larger deals. Consider a performance reserve held on Redwood balance sheet or via a trust; customers often prefer a neutral custodian.
- Termination gate: Accepting termination for 2 consecutive months is large risk. Prefer a staged gate: e.g., after 2 months trigger a remediation plan and extended cure (30 days), termination only after failure to comply with remediation plus one additional month.
- Negotiation levers: cap by ARR band, require mitigation steps (routing/failover), require joint post-mortem, limit LD to a fixed multiple (3x monthly) with annual cap.

Action items:
1) Vanessa — get committed monthly spend from Skyward.
2) Marissa — draft proposed redline (SLO Reserve + staged termination) to send back. Aim EOD tomorrow.

Marcus

Subject: Redwood counterproposal — SLO Reserve & staged termination (draft)

Elena / Tom,

Thanks for the details — we modeled the options and attached a draft term sheet (see attached "Proposed_Escrow_T&C.docx"). Summary of our counterproposal (high level):

- SLO Reserve: Redwood will place a performance reserve equal to 1.5 months of committed fees into a neutral custodian escrow for the initial 12-month term. Reserve size scales by ARR band; we modeled your indicated spend and attached the table.

- Draw mechanics: Reserve funds are only payable to Skyward after an investigation confirms a qualifying P1/P2 breach and Redwood fails to remediate within a 30-day cure period. Payouts are severity-indexed and do not exceed the reserve balance.

- Termination gate: Skyward may request termination for convenience if there are two qualifying months of P1 SLA misses within a rolling 3-month window AND Redwood fails to complete remediation within the 30-day cure period plus a 15-day remediation extension. If termination is exercised, the buyer receives a pro-rated refund of any prepaid fees plus a capped buyout equal to 3x the customer's monthly committed fees (capped at the escrow balance).

- Limits & safeguards: Total financial exposure (escrow + capped buyout) will never exceed 6 months of committed fees in any 12-month period. Redwood retains right to deploy mitigation (regional failover, dedicated pool) before any payout; joint post-mortem required for payout.

- Operational note: Setting up the escrow will add ~2–3 weeks; we recommend an escrow agent (we suggested Redwood Trust Partners in the doc).

We think this balances Skyward's desire for cash remedies with the need to limit systemic exposure and provide remediation. Please see the attached for legal redlines and track changes. Happy to hop on a call to walk through each bullet.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
